stages.label: Stage 1: Kana & Survival
stages.summary: Immediate arrival confidence: Hiragana & Katakana sound-script literacy, konbini checkout decoding, polite social cushioning, and rail-gate survival.

stages.label: Stage 2: JLPT N5
stages.summary: Core sentence architecture: Desu/Masu politeness, essential particles, Japanese counters, dining & hotel interactions, time expressions, and ~100 foundational Kanji.

stages.label: Stage 3: JLPT N4
stages.summary: Everyday independence: Te-form chains, casual plain speech, potential & volitional verbs, giving/receiving favors, conditional clauses, and ~300 Kanji.

stages.label: Stage 4: JLPT N3
stages.summary: Fluid social conversation: passive & causative-passive nuance, multi-clause storytelling, workplace rapport, regional ear-tuning, and ~650 Kanji.

stages.label: Stage 5: JLPT N2
stages.summary: Professional & media command: formal written connectors, full Sonkeigo/Kenjougo business honorifics, news & essay comprehension, and ~1,000+ Kanji.

stages.label: Stage 6: JLPT N1 (Full Fluency)
stages.summary: Unassisted native mastery: literary & classical grammar remnants, subtle rhetorical stance, four-character idioms (yojijukugo), and all 2,136 Jōyō Kanji.

units.title: Greetings, Konbini Survival & Everyday Politeness
units.subtitle: Time-of-day greetings, convenience store checkout decoding, essential signage, and polite social cushioning
units.communicativeGoal: Greet locals warmly, decode rapid konbini checkout questions, and respond calmly with お願いします and 大丈夫です.
units.grammarFocus: Set survival utterances, topic marker は in minimal requests, and polite 〜をお願いします frames.
units.culturalNote: Japanese convenience stores operate 24/7 with elevated clerk honorifics where a calm nod and two core responses handle every interaction.

units.title: Stations, IC Cards & Navigating Rail Lines
units.subtitle: Ticket gates, Suica/ICOCA top-ups, local vs. Shinkansen trains, exit navigation, and service disruption announcements
units.communicativeGoal: Read station gate and platform signs, top up IC cards, verify train stops, and locate numbered or directional exits.
units.grammarFocus: Location query どこですか, destination particle へ/に, and 〜に行きます / 〜で乗り換えます.
units.culturalNote: Urban Japanese stations integrate JR, metro, and private lines seamlessly via IC cards, with yellow signage marking exits vs. transfers.

units.title: Izakaya, Ramen Counters, Numbers & Ordering
units.subtitle: Party-size seating, ramen ticket machines, essential Japanese counters, allergy requests, and lively dining etiquette
units.communicativeGoal: State party size, read yen prices, order food and drinks using accurate counters, check allergens, and ask for the check.
units.grammarFocus: Counters 〜つ, 〜人, 〜杯, 〜本, 〜枚, existential あります, and 〜抜きでお願いします.
units.culturalNote: Ramen counters often use prepay meal-ticket machines (食券機), while izakayas serve a small お通し cover dish and settle one combined bill at the end.

units.title: Hiragana Mora Rhythm, Long Vowels & Pitch Essentials
units.subtitle: Mastering double consonants (っ), long vowels, contracted Yoon syllables, and clean mora timing
units.communicativeGoal: Distinguish minimal pairs like おばさん vs. おばあさん and きって vs. きて clearly in speech and listening.
units.grammarFocus: Moraic timing, Geminate っ (sokuon), palatalized きゃ/しゃ/ちゃ combinations, and question-rising intonation か.
units.culturalNote: Japanese rhythm gives equal beat length to every mora rather than stress-timing syllables like English.

units.title: Katakana Loanwords, Café Menus & Tech Vocabulary
units.subtitle: Decoding menus, hotel amenities, Wi-Fi prompts, and adapting English loanwords into natural Japanese phonetics
units.communicativeGoal: Order specialty drinks at kissaten and cafés, read Katakana signage, and pronounce loanwords so locals understand immediately.
units.grammarFocus: Katakana orthographic rules (ー long vowel bar, ファ/ティ/ヴ extensions) and noun-linking の.
units.culturalNote: Traditional 喫茶店 (kissaten) pair siphon-brewed coffee and thick toast sets with retro Katakana menu classics.

units.title: Self-Introductions, Origin & Polite Desu Identity
units.subtitle: Introducing yourself, sharing nationality and occupation, and exchanging names respectfully
units.communicativeGoal: Deliver a natural 初めまして self-introduction and ask polite getting-to-know-you questions without overusing あなた.
units.grammarFocus: Copula です / ではありません, topic particle は, inclusive も, and affiliation の (会社員・学生).
units.culturalNote: Addressing someone by family name + さん rather than second-person pronouns is fundamental to Japanese politeness.

units.title: Demonstratives Kore/Sore/Are & Department Store Shopping
units.subtitle: Pointing out items, asking to try on clothes, checking tax-free counters, and comparing colors and sizes
units.communicativeGoal: Ask staff to show items behind glass, check sizes in fitting rooms, and complete tax-free (免税) purchases.
units.grammarFocus: Ko-so-a-do series (これ/それ/あれ/どれ and この/その/あの/どの) plus 〜を見せてください.
units.culturalNote: Depachika (デパ地下) basement food halls beneath major department stores showcase regional confections and seasonal bento.

units.title: Clock Time, Days of the Week & Opening Hours
units.subtitle: Scheduling museum tickets, checking last-train times, reading calendar dates, and confirming reservations
units.communicativeGoal: Discuss schedules, verify museum admission cutoffs (最終入場), and catch the 終電 (last train).
units.grammarFocus: Time particle に, span markers 〜から〜まで, irregular minute/day readings (四時, 七時, 四日, 八日).
units.culturalNote: Many Japanese museums and shrines close doors 30 minutes before posted closing time—watch for 最終受付.

units.title: Existence Verbs Imasu vs. Arimasu & Street Directions
units.subtitle: Locating coin lockers, pharmacies, ATMs, and shrines using spatial nouns (上・下・隣・向かい)
units.communicativeGoal: Describe where people and landmarks are located and follow multi-step walking directions through neighborhood blocks.
units.grammarFocus: Animate います vs. inanimate あります, location particle に, and relational nouns (駅の北口の前に).
units.culturalNote: Japanese addresses number blocks and buildings by construction order rather than street names, making landmarks essential.

units.title: Daily Routines & Masu Verb Conjugations Across Time
units.subtitle: Present/future 〜ます, negative 〜ません, past 〜ました, and inviting friends with 〜ませんか
units.communicativeGoal: Talk about weekend plans and past trips, and extend warm invitations to meals or sightseeing.
units.grammarFocus: Polite verb inflections (ます / ません / ました / ませんでした), direct object を, and means/place particle で.
units.culturalNote: Inviting with negative question 〜ませんか ('Won't you join?') leaves graceful room for the listener without pressure.

units.title: I-Adjectives & Na-Adjectives: Weather, Seasons & Impressions
units.subtitle: Describing hot humid summers, autumn foliage, quiet temples, and past food or travel experiences
units.communicativeGoal: Express nuanced reactions to weather, scenery, and dishes across present and past tenses.
units.grammarFocus: い-adjective inflections (〜くない / 〜かった) vs. な-adjective inflections (〜じゃない / 〜だった) and degree adverbs.
units.culturalNote: Everyday Japanese small talk opens with seasonal sensitivity—cherry blossoms, rainy 梅雨, autumn 紅葉, or crisp winter air.

units.title: Ryokan Check-In, Onsen Etiquette & Polite Requests
units.subtitle: Te-form fundamentals: 〜てください, breakfast/dinner times, yukata sizing, and bathhouse rules
units.communicativeGoal: Check into a traditional ryokan, confirm dinner and private bath slots, and make polite room requests.
units.grammarFocus: Verb て-form construction across Godan, Ichidan, and irregular verbs; 〜てください and 〜てもいいですか.
units.culturalNote: At an onsen, guests wash thoroughly at seated showers before soaking and keep small modesty towels out of the mineral water.

units.title: Likes, Skills, Desires & Expressing Personal Interests
units.subtitle: Talking about favorite cuisines, music, sports, and travel bucket lists with 好き・上手・〜たい
units.communicativeGoal: Bond with locals over shared hobbies, deflect compliments humbly, and express what you want to see and eat.
units.grammarFocus: Subject-object が with 好き/嫌い/上手/下手 and desiderative verb stem + たいです.
units.culturalNote: When praised with 日本語が上手ですね, the natural Japanese response is a warm いいえ、まだまだです ('Not yet, still learning!').

units.title: Pharmacies, Clinics & Describing Symptoms Calmly
units.subtitle: Body vocabulary, explaining fevers or allergies, reading dosage instructions, and prohibition 〜てはいけません
units.communicativeGoal: Describe symptoms at a drugstore or clinic, understand medicine schedules (食後・一日三回), and follow health advice.
units.grammarFocus: Topic + part が痛いです, ongoing state 〜ています, obligation 〜なければなりません, and 〜なくてもいいです.
units.culturalNote: Japanese pharmacies distinguish OTC medications by class (第1類〜第3類医薬品), where a pharmacist explains Type 1 items directly.

units.title: Stepping Into Plain Speech: Casual Forms & Close Friendships
units.subtitle: Dictionary, Nai, Ta, and Nakatta forms for natural conversation with peers and reading quoted thoughts
units.communicativeGoal: Follow rapid casual banter among Japanese peers and switch cleanly between です/ます and plain style.
units.grammarFocus: Plain present/past affirmative and negative across verbs and adjectives; casual question drop intonation.
units.culturalNote: Shifting from です/ます to タメ口 (peer speech) reflects mutual closeness and shared age or cohort status.

units.title: Framing Opinions, Quotes & Indirect Questions
units.subtitle: Sharing thoughts with 〜と思います, relaying announcements with 〜と言っていました, and embedded clauses
units.communicativeGoal: State personal opinions softly, report what staff or friends said, and ask indirect questions.
units.grammarFocus: Plain form + と思います / と言っていました, plus embedded 〜か / 〜かどうか clauses.
units.culturalNote: Ending assertions with 〜と思います softens directness and invites collaborative agreement in Japanese conversation.

units.title: Relative Clauses: Describing People, Cafés & Hidden Gems
units.subtitle: Modifying nouns directly with plain-form clauses ('the bakery my friend recommended')
units.communicativeGoal: Specify exact places, items, and people in conversation without needing English-style 'who/which/that' pronouns.
units.grammarFocus: Pre-nominal relative clauses with plain verbs and Ga-for-Wa subject marking inside modifiers.
units.culturalNote: Neighborhood kissaten, shotengai arcades, and tiny Michelin Bib Gourmand counters are passed along by word of mouth.

units.title: Experiences,Weekend Variety & Changing Seasons
units.subtitle: Talking about life experiences (〜たことがあります), sampling activities (〜たり〜たり), and becoming (〜くなる/になる)
units.communicativeGoal: Share places you've visited, list varied weekend plans, and describe gradual changes in skill or weather.
units.grammarFocus: Past plain + ことがある, representative 〜たり〜たりする, and change-of-state 〜くなる / 〜になる.
units.culturalNote: Domestic travel around 47 prefectures—each prized for its own local 名物 (specialty dish)—is a favorite conversation opener.

units.title: Potential Verbs: What You Can Read, Eat, Speak & Reserve
units.subtitle: Expressing ability, venue rules, seasonal availability, and contrasting は vs. が in capability statements
units.communicativeGoal: Ask whether card payment, vegetarian menus, or late check-in is possible and discuss growing language skills.
units.grammarFocus: Potential verb formation (読める・食べられる), audible/visible 見える・聞こえる, and object particle が.
units.culturalNote: Distinguishing natural visibility from sightings (富士山が見える vs. 見られる) makes travel storytelling crisp.

units.title: Giving & Receiving Gifts, Souvenirs & Everyday Kindness
units.subtitle: Mastering あげる・くれる・もらう and the warmth of 〜てくれる / 〜てもらう favors
units.communicativeGoal: Express gratitude when locals walk you to a destination, offer regional omiyage souvenirs, and request help gracefully.
units.grammarFocus: Directional giving/receiving verbs (あげる/くれる/もらう) and benefactive auxiliary verbs (〜てあげる/〜てくれる/〜てもらう).
units.culturalNote: Bringing boxed regional お土産 back to coworkers or hosts after a trip strengthens social bonds across Japan.

units.title: Four Conditionals Demystified: と, ば, たら & なら
units.subtitle: Choosing the right 'if/when' for ticket machines, advice, future plans, and contextual recommendations
units.communicativeGoal: Give directions ('turn right and you'll see it'), ask for advice ('what should I do if...'), and respond to plans ('if you're going to Kyoto...').
units.grammarFocus: Natural-consequence と, hypothetical ば, sequential/universal たら, and contextual topic なら.
units.culturalNote: Recommending local spots with 京都に行くなら ('If it's Kyoto you're visiting...') signals attentive listening.

units.title: Intention, Resolutions & Advance Travel Preparation
units.subtitle: Volitional forms (〜よう), planning ahead with 〜ようと思う, and preparing in advance with 〜ておく
units.communicativeGoal: Share study or career goals, suggest spontaneous outings to friends, and talk about booking tickets ahead of Golden Week.
units.grammarFocus: Volitional conjugation, 〜ようと思っています, preparatory 〜ておく, and purposeful 〜ために / 〜ように.
units.culturalNote: During peak seasons like Golden Week, Obon, and New Year, reserving Shinkansen seats weeks ahead (予約しておく) is vital.

units.title: Transitive vs. Intransitive Pairs & Completed States
units.subtitle: Understanding ドアが開いている vs. 窓を開けてある in homes, trains, and shops
units.communicativeGoal: Describe whether reservations are already booked, lights are left on, or train doors are closing without sounding blaming.
units.grammarFocus: Transitive/intransitive verb pairs (開ける/開く, 閉める/閉まる, 決める/決まる) with 〜ている vs. 〜てある.
units.culturalNote: Japanese strongly prefers intransitive framing ('the ticket wasn't issued' / 'the schedule was decided') to preserve harmony.

units.title: Conjectures, Hearsay & Reading Visual Clues
units.subtitle: Distinguishing 〜そうだ (looks like / I heard), 〜ようだ, and 〜らしい in everyday life
units.communicativeGoal: Comment that food looks delicious, warn that rain is about to start, and share local news you heard.
units.grammarFocus: Stem + そうだ (appearance) vs. plain form + そうだ (hearsay), evidence-based 〜ようだ, and reliable 〜らしい.
units.culturalNote: Weather forecasts track the cherry-blossom front (桜前線) northward from Kyushu to Hokkaido every spring.

units.title: Causes, Soft Apologies & Nuanced Explanations
units.subtitle: Contrasting から, ので, and 〜て for tactful excuses, delivery updates, and unexpected outcomes (のに)
units.communicativeGoal: Apologize gracefully for delays or cancellations using soft ので and express mild surprise or regret with のに.
units.grammarFocus: Subjective から vs. polite objective ので, te-form cause constraints, and concessive のに.
units.culturalNote: Trailing off softly at ちょっと用事がありまして… lets a listener infer a polite decline without a blunt 'no'.

units.title: City Hall, Postal Services & Settling Into Neighborhood Life
units.subtitle: Parcel shipping (宅急便), address registration, recycling schedules, and polite counter requests
units.communicativeGoal: Ship luggage between hotels via Takkyubin, schedule redelivery, and understand municipal sorting guides.
units.grammarFocus: Honorific request 〜ていただけますか, time-slot specification, and compound nouns in civic life.
units.culturalNote: Luggage-forwarding services (宅急便) let travelers cross Japan hands-free with overnight delivery to their next hotel.

units.title: Passive Voice & Navigating Crowded Urban Life
units.subtitle: Direct passive, 'suffering' indirect passive, and objective event descriptions (〜で行われる)
units.communicativeGoal: Recount relatable mishaps (getting caught in rain, stepped on in rush hour) and understand festival announcements.
units.grammarFocus: Passive verb conjugation (〜れる/〜られる), adversity passive, and impersonal passive for public events.
units.culturalNote: Festivals (祭り) and fireworks (花火大会) are announced in passive voice to keep focus on the shared community event.

units.title: Causative & Causative-Passive: Permission, Requests & Tact
units.subtitle: Asking permission humbly with 〜させてください and expressing obligation with 〜させられる
units.communicativeGoal: Ask to take a day off, volunteer to handle a task (私にやらせてください), and discuss childhood or work obligations.
units.grammarFocus: Causative (〜せる/〜させる), contracted causative-passive, and 〜させていただく diplomacy.
units.culturalNote: Asking 'Please let me introduce myself' (自己紹介させていただきます) frames action as gratitude for the group's permission.

units.title: Conversational Flow, Aizuchi & Spoken Contractions
units.subtitle: Decoding 〜ちゃう/〜じゃう, 〜とく, 〜てる, active-listening cues, and trailing sentence-enders
units.communicativeGoal: Understand fast native dialogue at natural speed and keep conversations warm with well-timed 相槌 (backchanneling).
units.grammarFocus: Spoken contractions (〜てしまう→〜ちゃう, 〜ておく→〜とく, 〜なければ→〜なきゃ) and discourse markers なんか / やっぱり.
units.culturalNote: Frequent nods and soft 相槌 (なるほど、そうですね、へえ！) mean 'I'm attentively following you', not necessarily 'I agree'.

units.title: Festivals, Shrines, Temples & Cultural Storytelling
units.subtitle: Explaining customs with 〜という, defining terms (〜とは), and comparing Shinto and Buddhist traditions
units.communicativeGoal: Discuss omikuji fortunes, shrine etiquette, and regional traditions with curious visitors and Japanese friends alike.
units.grammarFocus: Naming/framing 〜というN, explanatory 〜というのは〜のことだ, and habitual 〜ものだ.
units.culturalNote: Two bows, two claps, and one final bow (二礼二拍手一礼) mark Shinto worship, while temple incense and quiet palms mark Buddhist visits.

units.title: Workplace Harmony, Horenso & Team Communication
units.subtitle: Reporting progress, flagging issues early, cushioning disagreement, and collaborative phrasing
units.communicativeGoal: Share status updates, consult colleagues before changing plans, and voice alternative ideas tactfully.
units.grammarFocus: 〜について / 〜に関して, tentative suggestion 〜のではないでしょうか, and 〜ようにする.
units.culturalNote: 報・連・相 (報告 report, 連絡 update, 相談 consult) underpins smooth teamwork in Japanese organizations.

units.title: Kansai-ben & Regional Ear-Tuning: Osaka, Kyoto & Kobe
units.subtitle: Recognizing ほんま, なんでやねん, 〜へん negation, おおきに, and Kansai pitch melody
units.communicativeGoal: Follow lively street food and comedy banter in Osaka and Kyoto while appreciating regional linguistic pride.
units.grammarFocus: Kansai copula や, negative 〜へん/〜ひん, progressive 〜とる, and gratitude おおきに.
units.culturalNote: Osaka's食い倒れ ('eat till you drop') food culture and warm conversational humor contrast playfully with Tokyo reserve.

units.title: Compound Verbs & Nuanced Aspect in Everyday Action
units.subtitle: Combining stems with 〜始める, 〜続ける, 〜終わる, 〜出す, 〜直す, and 〜忘れる
units.communicativeGoal: Express starting suddenly, redoing a draft, forgetting to tap out, or continuing a habit in compact single verbs.
units.grammarFocus: Masu-stem + aspectual/directional second verbs (降り出す, 書き直す, 乗り遅れる, 話し合う).
units.culturalNote: Japanese packs adverbial nuance into rich V1+V2 compounds rather than stacking separate adverbs.

units.title: Comparisons, Trends & Weighing Everyday Choices
units.subtitle: Proportional change (〜ば〜ほど), contrast (〜に対して / 〜一方で), and urban vs. countryside life
units.communicativeGoal: Discuss remote work, housing trade-offs, and lifestyle trends with balanced multi-perspective sentences.
units.grammarFocus: 〜ば〜ほど ('the more... the more'), 〜に比べて, 〜一方で, and 〜わりに ('considering that').
units.culturalNote: Revitalized historic kominka farmhouses and Shinkansen commuting have sparked fresh interest in regional 移住 (relocation).

units.title: Customer Inquiries, Returns, Exchanges & Problem Resolution
units.subtitle: Explaining mix-ups calmly, requesting receipts or exchanges, and understanding service apologies
units.communicativeGoal: Resolve billing errors, lost-and-found inquiries (忘れ物), or damaged items politely and effectively.
units.grammarFocus: Explanatory 〜んですが lead-ins, 〜ていただきたいのですが, and state-result 〜まま.
units.culturalNote: Station lost-and-found centers reunite commuters with umbrellas, wallets, and phones at remarkable rates.

units.title: Reading Columns, Reviews & Modern Essay Structure
units.subtitle: Written plain style (だ・である), sentence-linking Masu-stems, and summarizing main arguments
units.communicativeGoal: Read restaurant reviews, travel essays, and opinion columns comfortably without losing track of long sentences.
units.grammarFocus: Literary である copula, clause chaining via verb stems, and framing structures 〜というのは〜からだ.
units.culturalNote: Japanese essays often follow 起承転結—introducing, developing, pivoting to an unexpected angle, and synthesizing at the close.

units.title: Regrets, Relief, Expectation & Emotional Shading
units.subtitle: Expressing 〜ばよかった, 〜おかげで vs. 〜せいで, and 〜はずだ / 〜わけだ
units.communicativeGoal: Share hindsight lessons, credit teammates warmly with おかげで, and draw logical conclusions naturally.
units.grammarFocus: Counterfactual 〜ばよかった, attribution おかげで / せいで, logical 〜わけだ, and 〜わけではない partial negation.
units.culturalNote: Crediting success to others via おかげさまで reflects deep appreciation of mutual interdependence.

units.title: Film, Literature, Anime & Pop-Culture Discourse
units.subtitle: Discussing plot twists without spoilers, character voice pronouns (俺・僕・わし), and aesthetic reactions
units.communicativeGoal: Review books, films, and exhibitions with native friends and recognize stylistic role language (役割語).
units.grammarFocus: Emotive 〜ずにはいられない, 〜きっかけで, and role-specific pronouns and sentence particles.
units.culturalNote: Authors and screenwriters use 役割語 (role speech) to signal age, personality, and era instantly in dialogue.

units.title: Mastering Keigo I: Respectful Sonkeigo in Business & Hospitality
units.subtitle: Special respectful verbs (いらっしゃる・おっしゃる・召し上がる) and お〜になる structures
units.communicativeGoal: Address clients, professors, and honored guests with effortless, natural Sonkeigo without double-honorific errors.
units.grammarFocus: Suppletive Sonkeigo verbs, お + stem + になる, and avoiding 二重敬語 (redundant honorific stacking).
units.culturalNote: Japanese honorifics encode 'uchi-soto' (in-group vs. out-group): even your own company president is spoken of humbly to an external client!

units.title: Mastering Keigo II: Humble Kenjougo & Business Emails
units.subtitle: いたす・申す・伺う・拝見する, お〜する frames, and seasonal business correspondence
units.communicativeGoal: Write crisp Japanese business emails, schedule client visits, and open/close phone calls professionally.
units.grammarFocus: Kenjougo Type I (お/ご〜する, 伺う, 拝見する) vs. Type II (いたす, 申す, 参る) and cushion phrases (恐れ入りますが).
units.culturalNote: Opening an email or call with いつもお世話になっております acknowledges ongoing professional partnership.

units.title: Broadcast News, Headlines & Sino-Japanese Compounds
units.subtitle: Decoding condensed 2- and 4-Kanji news compounds, On'yomi patterns, and NHK-style lead sentences
units.communicativeGoal: Follow television news summaries and newspaper front pages on weather alerts, economics, and society.
units.grammarFocus: Headline nominalization (noun-ending clauses), 〜をめぐって, 〜に伴い, and 〜を受け.
units.culturalNote: Newspaper headlines omit particles and copulas into punchy Kango chains that unlock rapidly once you know On'yomi roots.

units.title: Science, Sustainability & Technological Innovation
units.subtitle: Discussing renewable energy, robotics, disaster resilience, and cause-and-effect chains
units.communicativeGoal: Read technical feature articles and debate environmental and urban-design solutions in structured Japanese.
units.grammarFocus: 〜に際して, 〜をきっかけに, 〜ざるを得ない, and 〜にほかならない.
units.culturalNote: From seismic base-isolation engineering to circular waste sorting (もったいない), precision engineering shapes daily Japanese life.

units.title: Formal Logic, Concession & Nuanced Debate
units.subtitle: Weighing competing viewpoints with 〜ものの, 〜にもかかわらず, 〜からといって, and 〜上で
units.communicativeGoal: Build persuasive, even-handed arguments in seminars or meetings while acknowledging counterpoints.
units.grammarFocus: Concessive 〜ものの / 〜にもかかわらず, prerequisite 〜上で, and warning against overgeneralization 〜からといって〜とは限らない.
units.culturalNote: Effective Japanese persuasion validates the counterpart's concern first (おっしゃる通りですが…) before introducing a counterpoint.

units.title: Contracts, Housing Leases & Official Civic Notices
units.subtitle: Understanding apartment terms (敷金・礼金・更新), municipal letters, and conditional stipulations
units.communicativeGoal: Read rental agreements, bank forms, and ward-office notifications without intimidation.
units.grammarFocus: 〜を問わず, 〜に限り, 〜次第 ('as soon as / depending on'), and 〜ものとする.
units.culturalNote: Traditional Japanese leases distinguish refundable security deposits (敷金) from key-money gratitude (礼金), though zero-zero listings are growing.

units.title: Idioms of Body, Nature & Craftsmanship (Shokunin Spirit)
units.subtitle: High-frequency figurative expressions (顔が広い・腑に落ちる・腕を磨く) in conversation and prose
units.communicativeGoal: Enrich spoken and written Japanese with vivid somatic and craft idioms that natives use daily.
units.grammarFocus: Idiomatic noun-verb collocations, 〜にかけては ('when it comes to'), and 〜だけのことはある.
units.culturalNote: The 職人 (shokunin) ethos celebrates quiet, lifelong refinement of a craft—from sushi knives to woodworking and software.

units.title: Demographics, Work-Life Balance & Contemporary Society
units.subtitle: Interpreting charts, survey data (〜割・〜を占める), and editorial discussions on modern Japan
units.communicativeGoal: Summarize statistical trends and participate in thoughtful discussions on education, aging, and work reform.
units.grammarFocus: 〜つつある (ongoing trend), 〜傾向にある, 〜にとどまらず ('not limited to'), and percentage/ratio framing.
units.culturalNote: Note that Japanese 割 (wari) represents tenths (3割 = 30%), a ubiquitous unit in news graphics and discounts.

units.title: Aesthetics: Wabi-Sabi, Architecture, Tea & Seasonal Arts
units.subtitle: Expressing subtle sensory impressions, onomatopoeia (擬音語・擬態語), and spatial harmony (間)
units.communicativeGoal: Describe textures, light, silence, and artistic craftsmanship using rich Japanese mimetics and aesthetic terms.
units.grammarFocus: Mimetic adverbs (しっとり・凛とした・ほっとする), 〜といったらありゃしない, and 〜かねない.
units.culturalNote: Japanese possesses over a thousand mimetic words (オノマトペ) that turn abstract feelings and textures into immediate sensory sound.

units.title: Presentations, Q&A Sessions & Executive Summaries
units.subtitle: Signposting talks, fielding tough questions gracefully, and synthesizing takeaways
units.communicativeGoal: Deliver a structured 5-minute presentation in Japanese and handle live audience Q&A with poise.
units.grammarFocus: Discourse signposts (冒頭で述べた通り・踏まえて), 〜を抜きにしては語れない, and 〜に先立ち.
units.culturalNote: Thanking the questioner (ご質問ありがとうございます) before answering sets a collaborative, composed tone in Japanese Q&A.

units.title: Modern Short Fiction, Narrative Voice & Subtext
units.subtitle: Reading contemporary Japanese fiction: unspoken emotion, shifting perspectives, and interior monologue
units.communicativeGoal: Read unabridged modern short stories while catching subtle emotional shifts and narrative irony.
units.grammarFocus: 〜かのようだ, 〜てたまらない / 〜てならない, and ellipsis of subjects across narrative paragraphs.
units.culturalNote: Modern Japanese fiction often conveys deep emotion through small seasonal details and pauses rather than explicit declaration.

units.title: N1 Gateway: Classical Remnants in Modern High Register
units.subtitle: Mastering 〜ず/〜ぬ, 〜べし/〜べからず, 〜ごとし, and 〜なり in editorials and formal prose
units.communicativeGoal: Decode classical grammatical echoes embedded in modern editorials, proverbs, legal notices, and speeches.
units.grammarFocus: Classical negative 〜ぬ/〜ん, obligation/prohibition 〜べし/〜べからず, and 〜んばかりに ('as if about to').
units.culturalNote: Classical bungo (文語) structures survive everywhere in modern signage ('入るべからず'), proverbs, and literary prose.

units.title: Yojijukugo: Four-Character Idioms in Leadership & Essay Writing
units.subtitle: Deploying 一期一会, 試行錯誤, 臨機応変, and 単刀直入 with precision and restraint
units.communicativeGoal: Understand and deploy high-impact four-character compounds naturally in speeches, essays, and negotiations.
units.grammarFocus: Syntactic integration of 四字熟語 with 〜な / 〜に / 〜する and 〜をもって.
units.culturalNote: Rooted in tea ceremony, Zen, and classical history, well-chosen 四字熟語 compress entire philosophies into four syllables.

units.title: High-Stakes Negotiation, Indirect Refusal & Diplomatic Tact
units.subtitle: Navigating 検討いたします, 〜いたしかねます, and preserving mutual face in complex agreements
units.communicativeGoal: Read subtle signals at the negotiation table and decline or counter-propose without friction.
units.grammarFocus: Polite impossibility 〜いたしかねます, 〜ないとも限らない, and 〜を踏まえた上で.
units.culturalNote: In Japanese business diplomacy, 前向きに検討いたします signals respectful deliberation rather than an instant 'yes'.

units.title: Philosophy, Psychology & Abstract Argumentation
units.subtitle: Unpacking dense academic prose, double negations, and epistemic modality
units.communicativeGoal: Read university-level essays and philosophical commentary while tracking multi-layered qualifications.
units.grammarFocus: 〜ないではいられない, 〜ともなると, 〜はおろか ('let alone'), and 〜にたる ('worthy of').
units.culturalNote: Double negatives in scholarly Japanese express measured intellectual humility rather than evasiveness.

units.title: Economics, Monetary Policy & Global Trade Commentary
units.subtitle: Reading Nikkei-level financial analysis, central bank statements, and market metaphors
units.communicativeGoal: Follow macroeconomic briefings, earnings analyses, and currency/trade reporting at native speed.
units.grammarFocus: 〜を余儀なくされる ('be forced to'), 〜相まって ('coupled with'), and 〜を皮切りに ('starting with').
units.culturalNote: Understanding fiscal-year rhythms (April 1–March 31 in Japan) contextualizes corporate budgets, hiring, and policy.

units.title: Legal, Civic & Policy Discourse
units.subtitle: Statutory phrasing (〜にあっては・〜を妨げない), public debate, and constitutional concepts
units.communicativeGoal: Comprehend policy white papers, civic referenda, and formal institutional announcements accurately.
units.grammarFocus: 〜に即して ('in accordance with'), 〜ない限り, 〜たりとも ('not even a single'), and 〜を禁じ得ない.
units.culturalNote: Modern Japanese civic vocabulary coined during the Meiji era (社会・権利・自由) shaped modern East Asian terminology.

units.title: Historical Narratives: Edo Townsfolk to Meiji Modernization
units.subtitle: Historical vocabulary, period drama (時代劇) registers, and cultural continuity
units.communicativeGoal: Enjoy museum placards, historical novels, and NHK Taiga dramas without needing subtitles.
units.grammarFocus: 〜に至るまで, 〜を経て, 〜ならではの ('uniquely characteristic of'), and historical honorifics.
units.culturalNote: Edo-period urban literacy, woodblock publishing, and merchant guilds laid deep foundations for modern Tokyo and Osaka.

units.title: Criticism, Irony, Humor & Rhetorical Stance
units.subtitle: Rakugo storytelling cadence, editorial wit, understatement, and 〜といったらない
units.communicativeGoal: Catch subtle humor, self-deprecating wit, and rhetorical questions in live talks and essays.
units.grammarFocus: 〜ではあるまいし, 〜とばかりに, 〜始末だ (critical outcome), and 〜に越したことはない.
units.culturalNote: In 落語 (rakugo), a lone seated storyteller conjures entire worlds using only a paper fan, a hand towel, and vocal register shifts.

units.title: Ceremonial Speeches, Toasts, Condolences & Life Milestones
units.subtitle: Weddings, farewells, seasonal letters (時候の挨拶), and deeply respectful ceremonial phrasing
units.communicativeGoal: Deliver a heartfelt ceremonial toast or farewell message and navigate delicate life milestones with grace.
units.grammarFocus: Elevated congratulatory & condolence formulas, 〜に堪えない (感謝に堪えない), and Imi-kotoba taboos.
units.culturalNote: Traditional formal letters open with a poetic nod to the micro-season before turning to practical matters.

units.title: Full Jōyō Kanji Synthesis: Rare Readings, Ateji & Homophones
units.subtitle: Distinguishing subtle homophones (勧める/進める/薦める) and reading unassisted literary Kanji
units.communicativeGoal: Choose exact Kanji nuances in writing and read dense unannotated Japanese texts effortlessly.
units.grammarFocus: Semantic differentiation of Kun/On homophones, Jukujikun (土産・紅葉・老舗), and 〜極まりない.
units.culturalNote: Selecting 老舗 (shinise, 'centuries-old shop') or 粋 (iki, 'understated chic') carries layers of cultural memory.

units.title: Crowning JLPT N1 Mastery: Unassisted Native Synthesis
units.subtitle: Seamless register switching across casual warmth, executive Keigo, and literary prose
units.communicativeGoal: Move fluidly between spirited neighborhood conversation, high-trust professional leadership, and unassisted native literature.
units.grammarFocus: Full-spectrum register calibration, pragmatic ellipsis, and synthesis of N5–N1 rhetorical architecture.
units.culturalNote: True Japanese fluency lives in 気配り—using language with attentive warmth so every person in the room feels respected and at ease.

stages.label: Stage 1: Sound, Compound Roots & Survival
stages.summary: Immediate Austrian & German confidence: clear pronunciation, Lego-style compound root splitting, polite greetings, Kaffeehaus & Beisl basics, and ÖBB transit signs.

stages.label: Stage 2: CEFR A1
stages.summary: Core building blocks: present-tense verb-second (V2) flow, modal verbs, nominative/accusative/dative cases, separable prefixes, hotels, directions, and daily routines.

stages.label: Stage 3: CEFR A2
stages.summary: Practical independence: spoken Perfekt storytelling, two-way prepositions, reflexive verbs, comparative adjectives, healthcare, housing, and subordinate clauses.

stages.label: Stage 4: CEFR B1
stages.summary: Natural social & workplace fluency: relative clauses, Präteritum vs. Perfekt register, passive voice, Konjunktiv II wishes, and Austrian conversational ear-tuning.

stages.label: Stage 5: CEFR B2
stages.summary: Nuanced professional & media command: two-part connectors, genitive prepositions, subjective modals, academic/news argumentation, and regional cultural depth.

stages.label: Stage 6: CEFR C1 (Full Fluency)
stages.summary: Complete native-level mastery: extended participial attributes, Konjunktiv I indirect discourse, Funktionsverbgefüge, Wiener Schmäh & literary prose.

units.title: Austrian Greetings, Kaffeehaus Essentials & Everyday Politeness
units.subtitle: Grüß Gott, Servus, Verlängerter, and navigating Viennese cafés & everyday shops
units.communicativeGoal: Greet locals politely, ask for everyday essentials, order in a Viennese Kaffeehaus, and settle the bill with confidence.
units.grammarFocus: Formal Sie vs. casual du greetings, noun gender articles (der/die/das), Ich hätte gern + accusative, and first compound splits.
units.culturalNote: Viennese Kaffeehäuser serve every coffee with a silver-tray glass of Alpine tap water and never rush guests with an unrequested bill.
units.austrianFocus: Grüß Gott, Auf Wiederschauen, Servus, das Sackerl, der Bankomat, ein Verlängerter, das Schlagobers, and das Beisl.

units.title: ÖBB Rail, Alpine Transit & Compound Word Roots
units.subtitle: Decoding Haupt·bahn·hof, Bahn·steig, and Schienen·ersatz·verkehr across Austria and Germany
units.communicativeGoal: Split long German transit compounds into clear root blocks, buy round-trip rail tickets, reserve seats, and navigate delays.
units.grammarFocus: Right-hand head gender in compounds, directional prefixes (Ein-/Aus-/Um-), separable transit verbs, and weil/obwohl/damit.
units.culturalNote: High-speed ÖBB Railjet and DB ICE networks connect Alpine and urban hubs seamlessly with open platforms and zero ticket turnstiles.
units.austrianFocus: ÖBB Bahnsteig (vs. DB Gleis), hin und retour (vs. hin und zurück), Ruhezone, and Austrian rail announcement phrasing.

units.title: Markets, Bakery Counters, Beisl Menus & Prices
units.subtitle: Semmeln, Erdäpfel, Paradeiser, Naschmarkt weights, and splitting the bill
units.communicativeGoal: Order rolls, produce, and Austrian classics by weight, check allergens, understand euro prices, and split or combine checks.
units.grammarFocus: Measure phrases without von, spoken euro numbers, dative experiencer schmecken, and seasonal adverb heuer.
units.culturalNote: Open-air markets like Vienna's Naschmarkt and neighborhood bakeries anchor daily shopping with fresh regional produce.
units.austrianFocus: Semmel, Erdäpfel, Paradeiser, Jause, Schweinsbraten, Deka (10g deli unit), prickelnd, Kren, Mehlspeisen, and heuer.

units.title: German Sound Craft: Umlauts, ß, ch-Sounds & Austrian Melody
units.subtitle: Crisp ä/ö/ü vowels, ich-Laut vs. ach-Laut, W/V/Z consonants, and soft Viennese cadence
units.communicativeGoal: Pronounce street names, Umlauts, and compound clusters cleanly while tuning your ear to soft Austrian consonants.
units.grammarFocus: Vowel length contrasts, final devoicing vs. southern lenis stops, and word-initial stress on separable vs. inseparable prefixes.
units.culturalNote: Spelling rules distinguish ß after long vowels/diphthongs (Straße, heißen) from ss after short vowels (Gasse, Wasser).
units.austrianFocus: Softer Austrian P/T/K articulation, vocalized -er endings, and -ig pronounced '-ik' in Austria vs. '-ich' in northern Germany.

units.title: Introducing Yourself, Countries, Languages & Sie vs. du
units.subtitle: Sharing where you come from, where you live, and navigating social formality smoothly
units.communicativeGoal: Introduce yourself warmly at events or hotels, talk about languages you speak, and read Sie/du cues accurately.
units.grammarFocus: Present tense of sein, kommen aus, wohnen in, sprechen (e→i vowel change), and W-questions vs. yes/no verb-first questions.
units.culturalNote: Using formal Sie with adults outside your friend circle signals mutual respect rather than coldness.
units.austrianFocus: Austrian academic and professional titles (Frau Magister, Herr Diplom-Ingenieur) and warm 'Ich bin der/die + Name' introductions.

units.title: Numbers to 1,000, Clock Times, Viertel über & Opening Hours
units.subtitle: 24-hour schedules vs. spoken half-past (halb vier = 3:30!) and Austrian quarter-hour conventions
units.communicativeGoal: Avoid the classic 'halb vier' trap, confirm appointment and concert times, and read shop opening plaques.
units.grammarFocus: Ordinal & cardinal numbers, um + clock time, am + weekday, and spoken half/quarter time expressions.
units.culturalNote: In German, 'halb vier' always looks forward to the upcoming hour—meaning halfway TO four (3:30), never 4:30!
units.austrianFocus: Eastern Austrian 'viertel vier' (3:15) and 'dreiviertel vier' (3:45) alongside 'Viertel nach / Viertel vor'.

units.title: Vienna U-Bahn, Trams (die Bim), Buses & City Wayfinding
units.subtitle: Validating KlimaTicket & 24h passes, asking locals for directions, and spatial landmarks
units.communicativeGoal: Navigate trams, metro lines, and historic old-town lanes on foot while understanding left/right/straight-ahead directions.
units.grammarFocus: Imperative Sie forms (Gehen Sie geradeaus, biegen Sie links ab) and contraction prepositions zum/zur.
units.culturalNote: Vienna's Wiener Linien network runs on trust-based proof-of-payment; paper single tickets must be stamped at blue Entwerter boxes.
units.austrianFocus: Die Bim (Viennese tram), Jahreskarte / KlimaTicket Österreich, die Stiege (stairwell/building wing), and ums Eck.

units.title: Alpine Gasthof & Hotel Check-In, Rooms & Breakfast Times
units.subtitle: Checking into city hotels and mountain inns, requesting extra pillows or keys, and Ortstaxe basics
units.communicativeGoal: Complete hotel check-in and check-out smoothly, ask about Wi-Fi and breakfast hours, and resolve small room needs.
units.grammarFocus: Possessive determiners (mein/Ihr/unser), es gibt + accusative, and negation with kein vs. nicht.
units.culturalNote: Family-run Alpine Gasthöfe and Pensionen often include hearty regional breakfast buffets and local transit guest cards.
units.austrianFocus: Der Polster (AT pillow vs. DE das Kissen), die Tuchent (AT down duvet vs. DE Bettdecke), and der Lift (AT elevator vs. DE Aufzug).

units.title: Weather in the Alps, Four Seasons & Packing Smart
units.subtitle: Forecasts from Danube sunshine to Tyrolean Föhn winds, clothing compounds, and small talk
units.communicativeGoal: Check mountain and city weather forecasts, shop for rain or winter layers, and chat naturally about the weather.
units.grammarFocus: Impersonal es expressions (es regnet, es schneit, mir ist kalt), temporal adverbs, and compound clothing nouns.
units.culturalNote: As the German saying goes, 'Es gibt kein schlechtes Wetter, nur falsche Kleidung'—layering (Zwiebellook) rules outdoor life.
units.austrianFocus: Die Haube (AT winter beanie vs. DE die Mütze), das Leiberl (AT T-shirt), and warm Alpine Föhn wind phenomena.

units.title: Emergencies, Pharmacies (Apotheke), Lost Items & Quick Help
units.subtitle: Finding night-duty pharmacies (Nachtdienst), reporting a lost wallet at the Fundamt, and urgent phrases
units.communicativeGoal: Ask for immediate assistance, find an open Apotheke after hours, and report lost passports, phones, or bags.
units.grammarFocus: Modal brauchen / helfen (+ dative), urgent imperatives, and clear descriptive color/material compounds.
units.culturalNote: Drugstores (Drogerien like dm or Bipa) sell toiletries and bandages, while only a red-cross/green-cross Apotheke dispenses medication.
units.austrianFocus: Austrian emergency numbers (Rettung 144, Bergrettung 140, Euro-Notruf 112), Verkühlung (AT cold vs. DE Erkältung), and Bankomat card blocking.

units.title: The Verb-Second (V2) Engine & Daily Life in Vienna and Berlin
units.subtitle: Keeping the conjugated verb anchored at Position 2 when fronting time, place, or objects
units.communicativeGoal: Describe your weekday and weekend routines fluidly without stiff subject-first monotony.
units.grammarFocus: Strict V2 main-clause word order, Time-Manner-Place (TMP) ordering, and stem-vowel-changing verbs (fahren, lesen, sehen).
units.culturalNote: Quiet hours (Nachtruhe and Sunday shop closures—Sonntagsruhe) shape a calm, restorative weekend rhythm across Austria and Germany.
units.austrianFocus: Austrian month & weekday nuances (Jänner in AT vs. Januar in DE; Samstag vs. northern Sonnabend).

units.title: Accusative Case Mastery: Shopping, Gifts & Direct Objects
units.subtitle: Why only masculine der→den / ein→einen changes, plus accusative prepositions (für, ohne, durch, um)
units.communicativeGoal: Buy gifts, groceries, and tickets while handling direct objects and accusative prepositions effortlessly.
units.grammarFocus: Accusative articles & personal pronouns (mich, dich, ihn, sie, es, uns), plus durch, für, gegen, ohne, um.
units.culturalNote: Bringing flowers (unwrapped before handing over!) or fine chocolates when invited to someone's home is cherished etiquette.
units.austrianFocus: Um + price ('um fünf Euro' in AT vs. 'für fünf Euro' in DE) and Austrian gift favorites like Mozartkugeln and pumpkin-seed treats.

units.title: Modal Verbs in Action: Können, Müssen, Wollen, Dürfen & Möchten
units.subtitle: Building the German sentence bracket (Satzklammer) for plans, rules, permissions, and abilities
units.communicativeGoal: Coordinate plans with friends, understand museum or alpine trail rules, and express wishes politely.
units.grammarFocus: Present-tense conjugation of all six modals + infinitive locked at clause end.
units.culturalNote: Clear signage on trails and public spaces uses 'Bitte nicht...' or infinitival 'Betreten verboten' rather than personal scolding.
units.austrianFocus: Austrian modal favorite 'mögen' in polite questions ('Magst du einen Kaffee?' vs. DE 'Möchtest du einen Kaffee?').

units.title: Separable & Inseparable Prefix Verbs: Unlocking Action Nuance
units.subtitle: Contrasting einkaufen, aufmachen, and anrufen with verstehen, bezahlen, and empfehlen
units.communicativeGoal: Talk about phone calls, grocery runs, opening windows, and getting recommendations with crisp sentence brackets.
units.grammarFocus: Separable prefixes (ab-, an-, auf-, aus-, ein-, mit-, vor-, zu-) vs. inseparable (be-, emp-, ent-, er-, ge-, ver-, zer-).
units.culturalNote: Answering the phone in German-speaking Europe traditionally starts by stating your surname clearly.
units.austrianFocus: Aufsperren / zusperren (AT unlock/lock with a key vs. DE aufschließen / abschließen) and sich ausgehen ('Es geht sich aus!').

units.title: Dative Case Foundations: Recipients, Locations & Mit/Nach/Zu/Aus
units.subtitle: Indirect objects ('giving whom what') and high-frequency dative prepositions (aus, bei, mit, nach, seit, von, zu)
units.communicativeGoal: Explain how you commute, how long you've lived or studied somewhere (seit + dative!), and whom you're meeting.
units.grammarFocus: Dative articles (dem/der/dem/den+n), dative pronouns (mir/dir/ihm/ihr/Ihnen), and present tense + seit for ongoing duration.
units.culturalNote: Saying 'Ich lerne seit drei Monaten Deutsch' uses present tense—because you are still learning right now!
units.austrianFocus: Zu Hause / daheim ('Ich bin daheim'—warm Austrian/southern standard for 'at home').

units.title: Family, Friends, Possessives & Describing People
units.subtitle: Talking about relatives, roommates, professions, and masculine/feminine job titles (-in)
units.communicativeGoal: Share stories about your family, partner, or colleagues with accurate possessive endings across cases.
units.grammarFocus: Possessive determiners (sein/ihr/euer—dropping inner -e- in eure!), feminine -in professions, and article omission with jobs.
units.culturalNote: Distinguishing 'ein Freund von mir' ('a male friend of mine') from 'mein Freund' ('my boyfriend') prevents classic misunderstandings!
units.austrianFocus: Austrian kinship warmth: der Bub (AT boy vs. DE der Junge) and das Mädel / Dirndl.

units.title: Apartments, Rooms & Two-Way Prepositions (Wechselpräpositionen)
units.subtitle: Where is it (Wo? = Dative) vs. Where is it going (Wohin? = Accusative) with in, an, auf, über, unter, neben
units.communicativeGoal: Describe apartment layouts, arrange furniture, and place items accurately on tables, walls, and shelves.
units.grammarFocus: Nine Wechselpräpositionen (an, auf, hinter, in, neben, über, unter, vor, zwischen) and posture pairs stellen/stehen, legen/liegen.
units.culturalNote: German floor numbering counts Erdgeschoss (ground floor) before 1. Stock (first floor upstairs—US second floor!).
units.austrianFocus: Das Vorzimmer (AT entryway/hall vs. DE der Flur), der Kasten (AT wardrobe vs. DE der Schrank), and der Polster.

units.title: Hobbies, Alpine Hiking, Skiing & Weekend Culture
units.subtitle: Expressing preferences with gern / lieber / am liebsten and planning outdoor excursions
units.communicativeGoal: Compare favorite pastimes, plan a hut-to-hut Alpine day hike or museum afternoon, and buy lift or exhibition passes.
units.grammarFocus: Adverbial preference scale (gern → lieber → am liebsten), treffen, and temporal prepositions vor/nach + dative.
units.culturalNote: Alpine clubs (ÖAV / DAV) maintain scenic mountain huts (Almhütten) welcoming hikers of every generation with soup and strudel.
units.austrianFocus: Schifahren / Skifahren, die Almhütte, die Brettljause, and greeting fellow hikers above ~1,000m with 'Servus' or 'Grüß dich'!

units.title: Supermarkets, Deposit Bottles (Pfand) & Everyday Errands
units.subtitle: Weighing produce, bakery self-service tongs, returning Pfand bottles, and post/parcel pick-ups
units.communicativeGoal: Breeze through Austrian and German supermarkets, bakeries, dry cleaners, and parcel lockers.
units.grammarFocus: Packaging & container nouns (eine Packung, eine Flasche, ein Glas), partitive pronouns (welch-/kein-), and imperatives.
units.culturalNote: Shoppers pack their own groceries rapidly at the checkout belt and bring reusable totes—don't block the scanner while bagging!
units.austrianFocus: Billa/Spar Feinkost deli counters (freshly made Semmeln on demand!), das Sackerl, and Austria's 2025+ Einwegpfand return system.

units.title: Concert Halls, Museums, Cinema & Cultural Invitations
units.subtitle: Booking Musikverein or Staatsoper tickets, coordinating meetups, and reacting to performances
units.communicativeGoal: Buy seated or standing-room concert tickets, arrange pre-show drinks, and talk about music, art, and film.
units.grammarFocus: Coordinating conjunctions without inversion (und, aber, oder, denn, sondern) and time-place meetup expressions.
units.culturalNote: World-class Viennese opera and symphony performances offer Stehplätze (standing-room tickets) for just a few euros.
units.austrianFocus: Wiener Staatsoper & Musikverein Stehplatz tradition, Garderobe coat-check rules, and Pausenbuffet spritzers.

units.title: Spoken Past Mastery: Perfekt Across Regular, Irregular & Prefix Verbs
units.subtitle: ge-...-t vs. ge-...-en participles, separable auf·ge·macht, and verbs in -ieren without ge-
units.communicativeGoal: Tell complete, natural stories about last weekend, vacations, and workdays in spoken German.
units.grammarFocus: Systematic past-participle formation (weak, strong, mixed, separable ge-infix, inseparable & -ieren zero-ge-) with haben vs. sein.
units.culturalNote: In everyday spoken conversation from Munich to Vienna, Perfekt carries 95% of past storytelling (except war/hatte/wollte/konnte).
units.austrianFocus: Austrian sein auxiliary with posture verbs: 'ich bin gesessen / gestanden / gelegen' (vs. northern DE haben).

units.title: Simple Past Anchors: War, Hatte & Modal Verbs in Präteritum
units.subtitle: Why native speakers say 'Ich wollte fragen' and 'Es war toll' instead of clunky modal Perfekt
units.communicativeGoal: Blend crisp Präteritum forms of sein, haben, and modals seamlessly into your spoken Perfekt stories.
units.grammarFocus: Präteritum conjugation of sein (war), haben (hatte), and modals (konnte, musste, wollte, durfte, sollte).
units.culturalNote: Mixing war/hatte/konnte with Perfekt action verbs ('Es war kalt, also sind wir ins Café gegangen') is the exact rhythm of native speech.
units.austrianFocus: Even in Vienna—where Präteritum of action verbs sounds bookish aloud—war and wollte/konnte are completely natural.

units.title: Reflexive Verbs: Morning Routines, Relaxation & Reciprocity
units.subtitle: Sich freuen auf vs. über, sich beeilen, sich treffen, and accusative vs. dative mich/mir
units.communicativeGoal: Talk about getting ready, looking forward to trips, remembering names, and catching up with friends.
units.grammarFocus: Accusative reflexive pronouns (mich/dich/sich/uns/euch) vs. dative reflexives when a body-part/clothing object is present ('Ich putze mir die Zähne').
units.culturalNote: 'Ich freue mich auf Freitag' looks forward to what's coming; 'Ich freue mich über dein Geschenk' rejoices over what already arrived!
units.austrianFocus: Sich ausgehen ('Geht sich noch ein Kaffee aus?' = 'Do we still have enough time/room for a coffee?')—Austria's #1 reflexive gem!

units.title: Comparisons, Superlatives & Choosing Hotels, Routes & Gear
units.subtitle: So ... wie, schneller als, am schönsten, and Umlaut shifts in kurz → kürzer → am kürzesten
units.communicativeGoal: Compare train connections, apartments, restaurants, and travel options clearly and persuasively.
units.grammarFocus: Equative (genauso ... wie), comparative (-er + als), superlative (am ...-sten / der ...-ste), and irregular gut/viel/gern.
units.culturalNote: Direct product and transit comparisons favor concrete facts (travel time, quietness, walkability) over hyperbole.
units.austrianFocus: Comparing Austrian Railjet vs. Westbahn private trains and regional Austrian wine & cheese styles.

units.title: Adjective Endings Without Tears: Der, Ein & Zero-Article Patterns
units.subtitle: Why 'ein guter Wein' and 'der gute Wein' follow one logical signal rule
units.communicativeGoal: Use descriptive adjectives before nouns naturally in menus, compliments, shopping, and emails.
units.grammarFocus: Strong, weak, and mixed adjective declension unified under the 'Someone Has to Show the Gender Signal' principle.
units.culturalNote: Regional designations act as uninflected -er adjectives: Wiener Schnitzel, Salzburger Nockerln, Berliner Luft!
units.austrianFocus: Viennese culinary & architectural phrases: ein kleiner Brauner, ein großer Gespritzter, Altbauwohnung.

units.title: Subordinate Connectors II: Wenn, Als, Dass & Indirect W-Questions
units.subtitle: Distinguishing one-time past 'als' from repeated/future 'wenn' and asking polite embedded questions
units.communicativeGoal: Recount childhood or first-arrival memories with als, frame conditions with wenn, and ask polite indirect questions.
units.grammarFocus: Als (single past event) vs. wenn (whenever/if) vs. ob ('whether'), plus verb-final indirect questions ('Wissen Sie, wann...').
units.culturalNote: Wrapping a question inside 'Können Sie mir sagen, ob...' immediately elevates counter and workplace politeness.
units.austrianFocus: Colloquial Austrian 'wie' heard for temporal 'als' in casual speech—recognizing it passively while using 'als' cleanly.

units.title: Doctor's Visits, E-Card / Insurance & Describing Health in Detail
units.subtitle: Booking appointments (Ordination vs. Praxis), explaining symptoms, sick notes, and recovery wishes
units.communicativeGoal: Schedule a medical or dental checkup, describe how long symptoms have lasted, and wish colleagues 'Gute Besserung!'.
units.grammarFocus: Modal sollen for doctor's advice ('Der Arzt sagt, ich soll...'), wehtun + dative, and temporal seit/vor.
units.culturalNote: Public statutory health insurance (ÖGK in Austria, GKV in Germany) covers clinic visits via chip card.
units.austrianFocus: Die Ordination (AT doctor's office vs. DE die Praxis), das Spital (AT hospital vs. DE das Krankenhaus), and Krankenstand.

units.title: Apartment Hunting, WG Interviews & Registering Your Address (Meldezettel)
units.subtitle: Decoding Altbau listings, Kaltmiete vs. Warmmiete/Betriebskosten, and municipal registration
units.communicativeGoal: Read rental ads, ask smart questions at an apartment viewing, and complete statutory address registration.
units.grammarFocus: Dative verbs (gefallen, gehören, passen), floor/area measurements (Quadratmeter), and polite email inquiries.
units.culturalNote: Both Austria (within 3 days via Meldezettel!) and Germany (Anmeldung) require registering a new residential address at the municipal office.
units.austrianFocus: Der Meldezettel, Betriebskosten, Garçonnière (AT studio flat), and Vienna's world-renowned Gemeindebau & Altbau housing.

units.title: Banking, Contracts, Subscriptions & Polite Customer Support
units.subtitle: SEPA direct debits, canceling contracts (kündigen), warranty claims, and formal emails (Sehr geehrte...)
units.communicativeGoal: Write clear customer-service emails, manage mobile or gym contracts, and verify notice periods (Kündigungsfrist).
units.grammarFocus: Infinitive clauses with um ... zu ('in order to') and ohne ... zu, plus formal letter openings and closings (Mit freundlichen Grüßen).
units.culturalNote: Many German and Austrian annual memberships auto-renew unless canceled in writing before the Kündigungsfrist.
units.austrianFocus: Erlagschein / Zahlungsanweisung, FinanzOnline, and Austrian consumer terminology.

units.title: Festivals, Advent Markets, Ball Season & Social Traditions
units.subtitle: Christkindlmarkt, Viennese Ballkultur, Fasching/Karneval, and seasonal greetings across the year
units.communicativeGoal: Join holiday gatherings, toast appropriately (Prost! vs. Zum Wohl!), and wish friends well across seasonal milestones.
units.grammarFocus: Prepositional verbs with da-/wo- compounds (ich freue mich darauf, worauf freust du dich?) and temporal clauses.
units.culturalNote: Eye contact when clinking glasses during 'Prost!' (beer) or 'Zum Wohl!' (wine) is taken seriously—never cross arms in a group toast!
units.austrianFocus: Wiener Christkindlmarkt, Punschstand, Wiener Ballsaison ('Alles Walzer!'), and 'Guten Rutsch!' into the New Year.

units.title: Relative Clauses Across All Cases & Prepositions
units.subtitle: Connecting rich descriptions smoothly ('die Stadt, in der ich lebe' · 'der Kollege, dem ich geholfen habe')
units.communicativeGoal: Describe people, places, and ideas precisely in multi-clause sentences without chopping speech into tiny fragments.
units.grammarFocus: Relative pronouns (der/die/das/denen/dessen/deren) in nominative, accusative, dative, genitive, and after prepositions.
units.culturalNote: Remember: relative pronoun gender/number matches the noun it refers back to, while its CASE comes from its job inside the relative clause!
units.austrianFocus: Describing Austrian UNESCO landmarks from Wachau river terraces to Salzburg's Altstadt and Hallstatt.

units.title: Written Narrative Past: Präteritum in News, Books & Biographies
units.subtitle: Recognizing strong and weak Präteritum (ging, kam, schrieb, entstand) in print and broadcasts
units.communicativeGoal: Read newspaper articles, museum placards, and novels effortlessly and recount historical biographies.
units.grammarFocus: Narrative Präteritum of strong/irregular verbs and Plusquamperfekt (hatte/war + Partizip II) for 'past-before-the-past'.
units.culturalNote: Knowing when to READ Präteritum (novels, Der Standard, Die Zeit) vs. SPEAK Perfekt (dinner table) marks true B1+ maturity.
units.austrianFocus: Reading Austrian quality press (Der Standard, Die Presse, ORF.at) and Habsburg-to-Republic historical timelines.

units.title: Passive Voice: Processes, Recipes, Architecture & Civic Rules
units.subtitle: Action passive (werden + Partizip II) vs. state passive (sein + Partizip II) and impersonal 'Es wird getanzt'
units.communicativeGoal: Explain how dishes are prepared, when buildings were restored, and how workplace or municipal processes run.
units.grammarFocus: Vorgangspassiv across tenses (wird gemacht / wurde gebaut / ist renoviert worden), Zustandspassiv, and passive with modals.
units.culturalNote: Recipes, manuals, and museum plaques rely heavily on passive voice and 'man' to keep focus on the craft or process.
units.austrianFocus: How classic Wiener Schnitzel (veal, souffléed in clarified Butterschmalz!) and Sachertorte are traditionally crafted.

units.title: Konjunktiv II Wishes, Advice & Unreal Conditions
units.subtitle: Wenn ich mehr Zeit hätte..., An deiner Stelle würde ich..., and past regrets (hätte ... gemacht)
units.communicativeGoal: Give tactful advice, brainstorm hypothetical scenarios, and express wishes or gentle hindsight without lecturing.
units.grammarFocus: Present Konjunktiv II (wäre, hätte, würde + Inf., könnte, sollte) and past counterfactual Konjunktiv II (wäre/hätte + Partizip II).
units.culturalNote: 'An Ihrer/deiner Stelle würde ich...' ('In your shoes I would...') softens advice far better than 'Sie müssen...'.
units.austrianFocus: Warm Austrian subjunctive softening in workplace and everyday counsel.

units.title: Workplace German: Job Applications, Interviews & Team Meetings
units.subtitle: CVs (Lebenslauf), strengths & experience, moderating meetings, and constructive feedback
units.communicativeGoal: Present your professional background clearly, contribute to German-language meetings, and follow up in writing.
units.grammarFocus: Fixed verb-preposition pairs (sich bewerben um, sich beschäftigen mit, beitragen zu, abhängen von) and nominalizations.
units.culturalNote: German and Austrian interviews value concrete examples and verifiable qualifications over exaggerated self-promotion.
units.austrianFocus: Austrian Kollektivvertrag (14 monthly salary payments including Urlaubsgeld & Weihnachtsgeld!) and Arbeiterkammer culture.

units.title: Nuanced Modal Particles: Doch, Ja, Halt, Eben, Mal & Eigentlich
units.subtitle: Decoding the emotional soul of spoken German—turning robotic sentences into idiomatic warmth
units.communicativeGoal: Hear and use unstressed modal particles to soften imperatives, express shared surprise, or signal friendly resignation.
units.grammarFocus: Pragmatic placement of doch, ja, mal, eigentlich, halt, eben, and wohl in middle-field syntax.
units.culturalNote: 'Komm mal kurz her!' sounds friendly and relaxed; 'Komm her!' without 'mal' sounds like barking an order.
units.austrianFocus: Austrian particle trio eh ('Das weißt du eh'), fei (Tyrol/Bavaria), and geh bitte! (affectionate disbelief: 'Oh come on!').

units.title: Austrian Regional Panorama: Vienna, Salzburg, Tyrol, Styria & Vorarlberg
units.subtitle: Ear-tuning across Austria's nine Bundesländer without losing Standard German clarity
units.communicativeGoal: Understand regional pronunciation and vocabulary shifts from Viennese melody to Alpine Tyrolean and Alemannic Vorarlberg.
units.grammarFocus: Diminutive suffixes (-erl, -l, -le), regional diphthongs, and code-switching between dialect coloring and Österreichisches Standarddeutsch.
units.culturalNote: Austria is pluricentric: Österreichisches Wörterbuch codifies official Austrian Standard German taught in schools and ministries.
units.austrianFocus: Nine federal states (Wien, Niederösterreich, Oberösterreich, Salzburg, Tirol, Vorarlberg, Kärnten, Steiermark, Burgenland) and signature greetings.

units.title: Travel Beyond the Guidebook: Wine Routes, Lakes & Thermal Spas
units.subtitle: Salzkammergut lakes, Wachau cycling, Therme wellness etiquette, and storytelling with temporal connectors
units.communicativeGoal: Narrate memorable travel experiences chronologically using bevor, nachdem, während, sobald, and seitdem.
units.grammarFocus: Temporal subordinating conjunctions—especially sequence-of-tense harmony with nachdem (Plusquamperfekt → Präteritum/Perfekt).
units.culturalNote: Central European sauna areas inside Thermen are traditionally textile-free quiet zones ('Ruhebereich — kein Schweiß aufs Holz!').
units.austrianFocus: Wachau Donauradweg, Salzkammergut Sommerfrische tradition, and Styrian Thermenland.

units.title: Media, Podcasts, Public Broadcasting (ORF / ARD) & Fact-Checking
units.subtitle: Summarizing audio reports, expressing agreement or skepticism, and quoting sources accurately
units.communicativeGoal: Follow German-language podcasts and evening news (Zeit im Bild / Tagesschau) and summarize stories to friends.
units.grammarFocus: Source attribution with laut + dative/genitive, zufolge (postposed!), and structured opinion frames (Meiner Ansicht nach...).
units.culturalNote: ORF's 'Zeit im Bild' (ZiB) at 7:30 PM and ARD's 'Tagesschau' at 8:00 PM are shared national touchstones.
units.austrianFocus: Ö1 radio documentaries, ZiB moderation style, and Austrian public-discourse vocabulary (Klubobmann, Nationalrat).

units.title: Debating Everyday Ethics: Mobility, Digital Privacy & Urban Living
units.subtitle: Structuring pros and cons, interrupting politely, and building consensus in group discussions
units.communicativeGoal: Hold your own in lively B1→B2 dinner or seminar debates on car-free city centers, cash vs. digital payments, and AI.
units.grammarFocus: Contrastive connectors (einerseits ... andererseits, zwar ... aber, im Gegensatz zu) and genitive noun chains.
units.culturalNote: Privacy awareness (Datenschutz) and valuing cash alongside cards remain deeply rooted civic instincts in Austria and Germany.
units.austrianFocus: Vienna's consistent #1 global livability rankings: social housing, 365-euro annual transit pass, and green-space planning.

units.title: Two-Part Connectors (Zweiteilige Konnektoren) & Rhetorical Flow
units.subtitle: Sowohl ... als auch, weder ... noch, nicht nur ... sondern auch, and je ... desto
units.communicativeGoal: Link complex ideas with crisp rhythmic balance in presentations, essays, and persuasive conversations.
units.grammarFocus: Correlative connector word order—especially verb-final 'je + comparative ..., desto/umso + comparative + V2'!
units.culturalNote: Well-structured correlative clauses give spoken arguments clarity without sounding academic or stiff.
units.austrianFocus: Discussing Austria's dual vocational apprenticeship & university education pathways (Lehre mit Matura).

units.title: Genitive Mastery & Formal Prepositions in Written Register
units.subtitle: Trotz, während, wegen, innerhalb, außerhalb, statt, and masculine/neuter -(e)s declension
units.communicativeGoal: Command crisp written and formal spoken German using high-register prepositions and clean genitive links.
units.grammarFocus: Genitive case across articles, adjectives, and N-declension nouns (des Studenten, des Kollegen, des Herzens) plus formal prepositions.
units.culturalNote: While casual speech famously swaps 'wegen dem Regen' (dative), confident B2/C1 writing and speeches shine with 'wegen des Regens'.
units.austrianFocus: Official Austrian administrative and journalistic genitive usage vs. relaxed Viennese dative speech.

units.title: Subjective Modal Verbs & Epistemic Nuance (Muss vs. Dürfte vs. Soll)
units.subtitle: Expressing 95% certainty ('Er muss im Zug sitzen') vs. cautious assumption ('Das dürfte stimmen') and hearsay ('Sie soll...')
units.communicativeGoal: Calibrate exact degrees of certainty, probability, and unverified rumor in professional and news discussions.
units.grammarFocus: Subjective modals in present and past (muss/dürfte/könnte/kann nicht + Partizip II + haben/sein) plus 'sollen' vs. 'wollen' claims.
units.culturalNote: 'Er soll reich sein' means 'People say he's rich'; 'Er will vor Ort gewesen sein' skeptically means 'He claims to have been there'!
units.austrianFocus: Austrian 'dürfte' as the polite journalistic favorite for cautious forecasts and estimates.

units.title: Passive Alternatives: Sich lassen, Sein + zu + Infinitiv & -bar Adjectives
units.subtitle: Saying 'Das lässt sich leicht lösen' and 'Das Problem ist kaum zu übersehen' like an idiomatic native
units.communicativeGoal: Replace heavy passive constructions with sleek, active-sounding German equivalents in meetings and writing.
units.grammarFocus: Modal passive substitutes: sich lassen + Inf., sein + zu + Inf., gehören + Partizip II, and productive -bar/-lich suffixes.
units.culturalNote: Native speakers prefer 'Das lässt sich einrichten!' ('That can easily be arranged!') 10-to-1 over 'Das kann eingerichtet werden'.
units.austrianFocus: Southern/Austrian 'Das gehört dringend repariert!' ('That urgently needs repairing!') construction.

units.title: Science, Climate, Alpine Glaciers & Clean Hydropower
units.subtitle: Nominal vs. verbal style: transforming dense noun phrases into clear spoken explanations and back
units.communicativeGoal: Read scientific and environmental journalism and present technical causes, consequences, and solutions fluently.
units.grammarFocus: Nominalstil ↔ Verbalstil conversion (Aufgrund des Anstiegs ↔ Weil ... angestiegen ist) and Future I/II conjectures.
units.culturalNote: Over three-quarters of Austria's electricity comes from renewable hydropower along the Danube and Alpine reservoirs.
units.austrianFocus: Alpine glacier monitoring (Pasterze am Großglockner), Nationalparks Austria, and Danube ecology.

units.title: Music, Visual Arts, Secession & Central European Cultural History
units.subtitle: From Mozart, Schubert & Mahler to Gustav Klimt, Loos, and contemporary Salzburg/Vienna stages
units.communicativeGoal: Discuss exhibitions, architectural movements, and musical performances with rich critical and historical vocabulary.
units.grammarFocus: Appositions in matching case, participial adjectives, and evaluative adverbs (bemerkenswert, wegweisend, umstritten).
units.culturalNote: The Vienna Secession's golden inscription—'Der Zeit ihre Kunst, der Kunst ihre Freiheit'—captures fin-de-siècle modernism in seven words.
units.austrianFocus: Wiener Moderne around 1900, Kunsthistorisches Museum, Albertina, and Salzburger Festspiele.

units.title: Business Negotiations, Project Proposals & Executive Presentations
units.subtitle: Structuring data-backed pitches, negotiating budgets and timelines, and summarizing action items
units.communicativeGoal: Lead a German-language client presentation, negotiate terms diplomatically, and write crisp protocol summaries.
units.grammarFocus: Concessive & conditional precision (sofern, vorausgesetzt dass, selbst wenn, ungeachtet + Gen.) and chart commentary verbs.
units.culturalNote: Punctuality, clear written agendas (Tagesordnung), and documented follow-ups build deep professional trust in DACH business culture.
units.austrianFocus: Navigating Vienna as an international headquarters bridge between Western and Central/Southeastern Europe.

units.title: Psychology, Communication & Navigating Conflict Constructively
units.subtitle: De-escalating misunderstandings, expressing empathy, and setting clear interpersonal boundaries
units.communicativeGoal: Address sensitive workplace or personal friction tactfully using 'I-statements' and nuanced modal framing.
units.grammarFocus: Subjunctive comparison 'als ob / als + Konjunktiv II' ('Er tut so, als wüsste er von nichts') and infinitive clauses with statt/ohne.
units.culturalNote: From Sigmund Freud and Viktor Frankl in Vienna to modern organizational coaching, German psychological vocabulary is unusually precise.
units.austrianFocus: Balancing German directness with Viennese diplomatic cushioning ('Ich würde meinen, dass...').

units.title: Contemporary Literature, Theatre & Film Across Austria, Germany & Switzerland
units.subtitle: Exploring DACH storytelling voices, stage dialogue, and film reviews
units.communicativeGoal: Read contemporary German-language novellas and critiques while appreciating stylistic voice across Vienna, Berlin, and Zurich.
units.grammarFocus: Free indirect speech (erlebte Rede), fronting for stylistic emphasis, and nuanced prefix pairs (durch·schauen vs. durchscháu·en).
units.culturalNote: Variable-stress verbs (úm·fahren 'knock over' vs. umfáh·ren 'drive around'!) reward attentive prosody.
units.austrianFocus: Vienna's Burgtheater ('die Burg') tradition and modern Austrian literary voices from Stefan Zweig and Ingeborg Bachmann onward.

units.title: B2 Capstone: Complex Argumentative Essays & Spontaneous Panel Debate
units.subtitle: Synthesizing multiple sources, steel-manning opposing views, and speaking coherently under time pressure
units.communicativeGoal: Deliver a structured 4-minute extemporaneous argument and write cohesive editorial-level German prose.
units.grammarFocus: Cohesion devices (darüber hinaus, demgegenüber, infolgedessen, nichtsdestotrotz) and tight clause architecture.
units.culturalNote: German academic and editorial style prizes Sachlichkeit—letting structured evidence carry persuasion rather than emotional exaggeration.
units.austrianFocus: Austrian Matura & ÖSD B2/C1 rhetorical expectations alongside Goethe-Zertifikat standards.

units.title: C1 Gateway: Extended Participial Attributes (Linksattribute) Unpacked
units.subtitle: Reading and crafting dense pre-nominal modifiers in law, journalism, rail, and scholarship
units.communicativeGoal: Parse four-line German noun brackets on the first pass in reading and listening, and deploy compact modifiers in formal writing.
units.grammarFocus: Present participle (Partizip I), past participle (Partizip II), and modal gerundive (zu + Partizip I: 'ein ernst zu nehmender Einwand').
units.culturalNote: The gerundive 'eine kaum zu überschätzende Bedeutung' compresses an entire modal passive relative clause into four crisp words.
units.austrianFocus: Unpacking official Austrian ministry, university, and ÖBB institutional prose effortlessly.

units.title: Konjunktiv I: Journalistic Neutrality & Indirect Discourse
units.subtitle: Reporting speeches, court testimony, and press conferences with er sei, sie habe, man werde
units.communicativeGoal: Read quality German-language newspapers with full sensitivity to speaker distance and report statements neutrally.
units.grammarFocus: Konjunktiv I formation across tenses (sei, habe, komme; sei gekommen, habe gesagt) and fallback to Konjunktiv II when forms collide.
units.culturalNote: Konjunktiv I does NOT signal doubt—it marks scrupulous journalistic neutrality that attributes claims cleanly to their speaker.
units.austrianFocus: Comparing Konjunktiv I reporting in ORF Zeit im Bild, Der Standard, Süddeutsche Zeitung, and NZZ.

units.title: Funktionsverbgefüge: Institutional & Academic Precision
units.subtitle: Zur Verfügung stellen, in Anspruch nehmen, in Frage stellen, and eine Entscheidung treffen
units.communicativeGoal: Upgrade plain B1 verbs into idiomatic C1 noun-verb collocations in professional reports, lectures, and correspondence.
units.grammarFocus: Productive light-verb constructions (bringen/kommen/stellen/ziehen/nehmen + prepositional noun) and negation placement before the PP.
units.culturalNote: Distinguishing 'in Frage kommen' ('to be a viable option') from 'in Frage stellen' ('to call into question') is hallmark C1 command.
units.austrianFocus: In Evidenz halten ('keep on file/mindful of') and urgenzieren / urgieren—distinctive high-register Austrian administrative verbs.

units.title: Derivational Prefix Mastery: Ver-, Zer-, Ent-, Er-, Be- & Miss-
units.subtitle: Multiplying your active C1 vocabulary 5× by feeling the semantic logic of verbal and nominal prefixes
units.communicativeGoal: Infer unfamiliar C1 words on sight and distinguish subtle cousins like erkennen, anerkennen, verkennen, and bekennen.
units.grammarFocus: Semantic patterns of inseparable prefixes (ent- removal/emergence, ver- transformation/error, zer- fragmentation, er- achievement).
units.culturalNote: A single root like 'stellen' yields vorstellen, einstellen, ausstellen, verstellen, erstellen, unterstellen, and bereitstellen!
units.austrianFocus: Austrian legal and administrative derivatives (angeloben, Kundmachung, Verlassenschaft, Pragmatisierung).

units.title: Economics, European Policy & Social Partnership (Sozialpartnerschaft)
units.subtitle: Macroeconomics, collective bargaining, fiscal debates, and reading central-bank & EU analyses
units.communicativeGoal: Engage fluently in executive and policy discussions on inflation, trade, energy transition, and labor models.
units.grammarFocus: Advanced causal/instrumental prepositions (angesichts, infolge, mangels, zwecks, anhand, zugunsten) + genitive.
units.culturalNote: Austria's post-war Sozialpartnerschaft brings chambers of labor, business, and agriculture together to negotiate consensus before strikes arise.
units.austrianFocus: Wirtschaftskammer (WKÖ), Arbeiterkammer (AK), Nationalbank commentary, and DACH economic terminology.

units.title: Law, Civic Institutions, Federalism & Officialese (Amtsdeutsch)
units.subtitle: Translating dense statutory and municipal letters into plain human action steps
units.communicativeGoal: Read tax notices, notary deeds, and civic ordinances with calm clarity without needing a translator.
units.grammarFocus: Unintroduced conditional clauses (verb-first 'Sollte die Frist verstreichen,...'), 'sofern nicht', and nominalized chains.
units.culturalNote: Fronting 'Sollte...' or 'Wäre...' in position 1 drops 'wenn' completely—creating sleek, high-register conditional elegance.
units.austrianFocus: Austrian civic terms: Bezirkshauptmannschaft, Magistrat, Bescheid, Erlagschein, and Bundes-Verfassungsgesetz.

units.title: Philosophy, Intellectual History & Essayistic German (Wissenschaftssprache)
units.subtitle: Reading Kant-to-Wittgenstein clarity, seminar discourse, hedging, and precision definitions
units.communicativeGoal: Follow university lectures, podcasts, and long-form essays in the humanities and sciences at native speed.
units.grammarFocus: Epistemic hedging (es liegt nahe, dass...; insofern ... als; es sei denn, dass...) and abstract noun formation (-heit/-keit/-ung/-ität).
units.culturalNote: Ludwig Wittgenstein's Viennese aphorism—'Die Grenzen meiner Sprache bedeuten die Grenzen meiner Welt'—celebrates crystal-clear thought.
units.austrianFocus: The Vienna Circle (Wiener Kreis), University of Vienna seminar traditions, and Austrian intellectual prose.

units.title: Wiener Schmäh, Cabaret (Kabarett), Irony & Register Play
units.subtitle: Decoding dry satire, understatement, double meanings, and classic Viennese & German Kabarett
units.communicativeGoal: Catch subtle irony, humor, and cultural allusions in live comedy, theatre, and witty dinner-party banter.
units.grammarFocus: Litotes ('nicht ganz unproblematisch'), rhetorical particles, ellipsis, and deliberate high/low register juxtaposition.
units.culturalNote: Political and social Kabarett in Vienna, Munich, and Berlin blends razor-sharp linguistic wordplay with affectionate self-irony.
units.austrianFocus: From Karl Kraus and Helmut Qualtinger to modern Austrian Kabarett—how Wiener Schmäh defuses tension with charm.

units.title: Idiomatic Mastery, Proverbs & Metaphorical Precision
units.subtitle: Deploying Redewendungen (auf den Punkt bringen, über seinen Schatten springen, den Nagel auf den Kopf treffen)
units.communicativeGoal: Use figurative idioms and proverbs with native accuracy, tone sensitivity, and effortless timing.
units.grammarFocus: Fixed syntactic idioms, metaphorical dative possessors ('Das liegt mir am Herzen'), and register-matched paraphrase.
units.culturalNote: Well-placed idioms make C1 speech vivid and memorable; overusing textbook proverbs back-to-back sounds unnatural—restraint wins.
units.austrianFocus: Beloved Austrian idioms: 'Das geht sich ums Arschlecken / haarscharf aus', 'Da fährt die Eisenbahn drüber!' ('No arguing with that!').

units.title: Crowning CEFR C1 Fluency: Pluricentric Command Across Vienna, Berlin & Zurich
units.subtitle: Effortless switching between warm Austrian regional authenticity, crisp Standard German, and literary prose
units.communicativeGoal: Speak, read, negotiate, joke, and write across any social, academic, or professional setting in the German-speaking world.
units.grammarFocus: Full-spectrum stylistic synthesis: cadence, register modulation, Konjunktiv I/II, participial elegance, and pluricentric awareness.
units.culturalNote: Mastery of pluricentric German means honoring local identity in Vienna, Salzburg, Munich, Berlin, or Zurich with equal grace.
units.austrianFocus: Complete command of Österreichisches Deutsch alongside Bundesdeutsch—knowing every nuance and feeling at home everywhere.
